# Tobit Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Tobit ended his words of praise. He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight, and after eight years he recovered it; and he gave alms and continued fearing the Lord his God and giving thanks to him.

**2** And when he had grown very old, he called his son and the six grandsons and said to them, "My child, take your sons.

**3** See, I have grown old and am ready to depart from life. Go to Media, my child, for I believe all the words of Nahum the prophet concerning Nineveh: that everything will be fulfilled and will overtake Assyria and Nineveh — all that the prophets of Israel spoke, whom God sent.

**4** Not one of those words will fall short; everything will happen at its appointed time. And in Media it will be safer than in Assyria and Babylon. For I know and believe that everything God has spoken will be fulfilled and will come to pass, and not one word of the prophecies will fail.

**5** All our kindred who dwell in the land of Israel will be scattered and taken captive from the good land, and all the land of Israel will become a wasteland — and Samaria and Jerusalem will become a wasteland — and the house of God will lie in sorrow and will be burned for a time.

**6** "But God will again have mercy on them and bring them back to the land of Israel; and they will rebuild the house, though not as the former one, until the time when the appointed season is fulfilled. And after these things they will all return from their captivity and will rebuild Jerusalem with honor, and the house of God will be rebuilt in it, as the prophets of Israel spoke concerning it.

**7** And all the nations throughout the whole earth will turn and fear God in truth; all of them will abandon their idols, which have led them into error, and will bless the God of the ages in righteousness.

**8** All the sons of Israel who are saved in those days, remembering God in truth, will be gathered together and will come to Jerusalem and will dwell forever in the land of Abraham in safety, and it will be given over to them. And those who love God in truth will rejoice, and those who commit sin and unrighteousness will be absent from all the earth.

**9** "Now then, my children, I command you: serve God faithfully and do what is pleasing before him; and command your children also to do righteousness and to give alms, to be mindful of God and to bless his name at all times sincerely and with all their strength.

**10** Now, my child, leave Nineveh, for what Nahum said will surely come to pass. But go to Media, for there it will be safe. From my youth I trusted Ahikar, and he helped me until I reached old age. Remember what he did to Nadan, the son of his brother? He dragged him down into the earth, but Ahikar himself came up into the light. Ahikar gave alms and was saved from the deadly snare that Nadan had set for him; but Nadan walked into the snare of death and it destroyed him.

**11** Now then, my children — see what almsgiving does, and what unrighteousness does: it kills! But now my soul is ready to depart."

**12** And they laid him on his bed, and he died and was buried honorably.

**13** And when his mother Anna died, Tobias buried her with his father. Then Tobias departed with his wife and children to Ecbatana, to his father-in-law Raguel.

**14** He grew old with honor, and he buried his parents-in-law with honor, and he inherited their estate and the estate of his father Tobit.

**15** And he died in Ecbatana of Media, being ninety-nine years old. And he saw and heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus had captured; and before his death he rejoiced over Nineveh.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

The final chapter brings three narrative threads to resolution: Tobit's death (vv. 1–2, 12), his deathbed prophecy (vv. 3–11), and Tobias's concluding life and witness of Nineveh's fall (vv. 13–15).

**Nahum vs. Jonah:** Codex Sinaiticus names Nahum (*Nahoum*) as the prophet whose words Tobit trusts. This is a significant textual note — some manuscript traditions read Jonah, and modern readers might expect Jonah (who also prophesied against Nineveh). The Sinaiticus reading is preserved here without harmonization.

**Age figures (Sinaiticus):** Tobit loses sight at 58, regains at 66, dies at 112 (implied from the narrative). Tobias dies at 99. These figures differ in Vaticanus (158 and 127 respectively). I follow Sinaiticus (GII) as the base text.

**Verse 10 — Ahikar:** The story of Ahikar and his nephew Nadan (or Nadab) is a cross-reference to the ancient Ahikar wisdom tale, a widely-circulating Aramaic/Assyrian story in which the wise counselor Ahikar is betrayed by his adopted son Nadan but ultimately vindicated. The moral parallel to Tobit's own story (faithful suffering rewarded) is pointed.

**Verse 11:** The final moral (*thelēma*) of the entire book is spoken from a deathbed: almsgiving saves; unrighteousness destroys. This is the theological thesis of Tobit rendered as last words.

— LOGOS
